To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sunlight exclusion affects gene expression of berry skin in two different red grape cultivars (Vitis Vinifera L.) in which anthocyanin synthesis is sunlight-dependent or -independent.

sunlight exclusion from fruiting clusters of red grapes induces differential gene expression in the berry skin, which may be related to the differential responses of anthocyanin synthesis to sunlight in the two cultivar.

the berry skin of the red grape cultivar ‘Jingyan’, in which anthocyanin synthesis is sunlight-independent, has a simpler gene response to sunlight exclusion from fruiting than does the skin of ‘Jingyi’, in which anthocyain synthesis is sunlight-dependent.

the genetic background responsible for the different anthocyanin accumulation patterns of ‘Jingyan and Jingxiu’ in response to sunlight exclusion.
the genetic basis of sunlight-dependent and -independent anthocyain biosynthesis in berry skins of two red grape (Vitis vinfera) cultivars.
the molecular basis of sunlight-dependent anthocyanin synthesis in berry skin, which will be useful for improving the quality of grape berries.

the genetic background and the light signal system are both important for sunlight-dependent anthocyanin synthesis in grape berry skin.
sunlight exclusion induces a complex and diverse response in ‘Jingyi’ berry skin, whereas it causes a more limited and simple response in the skin of ‘Jingyan’.

the sunlight-dependent anthocyanin accumulation in the berry skin is the result of a complex network of gene transcriptional changes, including those involved in light perception, phytohormone signaling, ubiquitin-dependent protein proteolysis, and flavonoid biosynthesis.

the transcriptional changes in the skin of ‘Jingyan’, a cultivar that can synthesize anthocynanins after sunlight exclusion, are less complex than those in ‘Jingyu’, a cultivar which cannot synthesize anthocianins after sunlight exclusion.
